note: Set B is better because it preserves scientific notation (E+9) in stiffness values, whereas Set A frequently strips the exponent, making values orders of magnitude wrong (e.g., 115.82 vs 115.82E+9). Set A also contains several hallucinated values (TwGJStiff 134.15, Height 28.34) and incorrect units (Inertia in kg/m). Set B has fewer errors overall, though it includes a significant mass truncation (347 kg) and mislabels mass center as height.
remarks: Both sets struggle with TMassDen at Elevation 0.0 (reading ~556 instead of 5590.87). Set A's systematic removal of exponents from stiffness values is a critical failure for engineering data.
